requirements.requirement: node1 (router) hands out DHCP addresses on the private network shared by node2 and node3
requirements.summary: node1's eth1 was configured as 192.168.50.1/24 (cmd-991d60513d4741fc), a dhcp.private UCI section with pool 100-199 was created and dnsmasq restarted with UDP/67 confirmed listening (cmd-7d3f293962544196, cmd-47c74a3c31f14db6). node2 and node3 subsequently obtained real DHCP leases (192.168.50.50 and 192.168.50.175) on their private-network NICs, and node1's own lease file recorded both (cmd-4b5098aeba7d435d, cmd-03c6535c823a4abe, cmd-a57c73ac8e314ad3).

requirements.requirement: node2 always receives the same address across repeated leases
requirements.summary: A static DHCP host reservation (MAC 02:70:a4:8a:94:63 -> 192.168.50.50) was added (cmd-7d3f293962544196). node2's connection was cycled down/up twice and obtained 192.168.50.50 both times (cmd-4b5098aeba7d435d, cmd-e6c9bebb5ea34318), confirmed in node1's lease file (cmd-a57c73ac8e314ad3). A third confirmation after a full node2 reboot again shows 192.168.50.50 (cmd-d40df80c4b254249, cmd-ddcb9e3d7d914de3), giving strong repeated-lease evidence.

requirements.requirement: node3 is addressed from the general dynamic pool (not statically reserved)
requirements.summary: No static host entry exists for node3's MAC; node3 obtained 192.168.50.175, within the configured dynamic pool range (100-199 offset from 192.168.50.1), confirmed both in its own interface state and in node1's dhcp.leases file (cmd-03c6535c823a4abe, cmd-a57c73ac8e314ad3), and again after a full reboot (cmd-678e3ca6ec594827, cmd-ddcb9e3d7d914de3).

requirements.requirement: node1 provider-wide restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 0a606a54 with eth1 up and dnsmasq running was captured (cmd-a3bd588498674e67, global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity). A reboot was issued (cmd-8b664c5b5d9c41ff, after a failed first attempt using an unavailable nohup binary); SSH was unreachable during the transition (cmd-e9aa15c23a3c4342) and then reconnected with a new boot_id fc65e761 and uptime reset (cmd-dbf6e22b179548b0, global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity). Post-restart state shows the UCI network/dhcp config, static host entry, and running dnsmasq intact, with port 67 again listening (cmd-4ff19f9dd7d44ecd, cmd-156767617c22475c).

requirements.requirement: node2 provider-wide restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 6aa805ba with enp8s0 leased at .50 was captured (cmd-55b968ec439a41f8). systemctl reboot was issued (cmd-7aa37707b8fc4158); connection was unreachable during transition (cmd-c6771bd0b3014292, cmd-439c24c26f7947cd) and then reconnected with new boot_id 949b7f8b (cmd-f8f2edd14dda4ae9). node2 reacquired its reserved address 192.168.50.50 post-restart (cmd-d40df80c4b254249), matching node1's lease file (cmd-ddcb9e3d7d914de3).

requirements.requirement: node3 provider-wide restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id c2f29441 with enp8s0 leased at .175 was captured (cmd-8aef1392fe1c45ca). systemctl reboot was issued (cmd-c8b720ae1f034984); connection was unreachable during transition (cmd-aa290a47fdf94cc6, cmd-004f6d2390414f44) and reconnected with new boot_id cf03d382 (cmd-d745c3591e7846af). node3 reacquired a pool address 192.168.50.175 post-restart (cmd-678e3ca6ec594827), matching node1's lease file (cmd-ddcb9e3d7d914de3).

overall_summary: All three material outcomes are directly and repeatedly demonstrated: node1 serves DHCP on the shared private network, node2 consistently receives its reserved 192.168.50.50 across multiple lease cycles and a reboot, and node3 is addressed from the dynamic pool (192.168.50.175) and reconfirmed after reboot. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was executed on all three nodes with clean before/restart/after boot-identity transitions and confirmed recovery of DHCP configuration, service state, and address assignments. Hygiene is good; the only imperfect step was a failed reboot attempt on node1 using an unavailable 'nohup' binary, which caused no state change and was promptly corrected.
limitations: The first node1 reboot attempt (cmd-6e8aaf655c0a40f4) reported success but 'nohup' was not found on this busybox image, so no reboot actually occurred until retried; this is a minor discovery/troubleshooting artifact, not a functional gap.

Lease repeatability was validated via connection down/up cycles and a full reboot rather than by exhausting/renewing an actual DHCP lease timer, which is an accepted proxy but not a lease-expiry-based renewal test.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands map clearly to the task or restart protocol: UCI network/dhcp interface and pool config (cmd-991d60513d4741fc, cmd-7d3f293962544196), firewall zone addition plus dnsmasq restart to actually serve DHCP on the new zone (cmd-47c74a3c31f14db6), NetworkManager reapply/up/down cycles on node2/node3 to bring up the private NIC and validate lease behavior (cmd-9d3d54a99bf64f67, cmd-047aa7d9f7274430, cmd-4b5098aeba7d435d, cmd-03c6535c823a4abe, cmd-e6c9bebb5ea34318), and the three node reboots required by the restart-evidence protocol (cmd-8b664c5b5d9c41ff, cmd-7aa37707b8fc4158, cmd-c8b720ae1f034984). One reboot attempt on node1 using 'nohup' failed outright (binary not found, no reboot occurred) and was immediately retried with a working invocation (cmd-6e8aaf655c0a40f4); since it produced no state change it is not scored as an unnecessary mutation, only noted. Firewall/network diff snapshots show only the intended new eth1/dnsmasq listeners and expected post-reboot PID/ephemeral differences, with no abandoned files, failed services, or weakened security controls.
